title: Archify: click your codebase
musicPrompt: Sleek, curious product-launch bed for a 75-second tech short, about 100 BPM, soft analog synth pulses, warm sub bass, crisp light hi-hats and glassy plucks, a small lift around 50 seconds and a calm resolve into the end card, instrumental, no vocals.

scenes.text: Ask Claude how your app works, and get a clickable map that links to the exact lines of code.
Welcome to Claude Skills, by Curiously.
This is Archify. Ask it about one feature of your repo. It reads the real code, and its architecture boxes can open the files and lines behind them.
scenes.say: This is Arkify. Ask it about one feature of your repo. It reads the real code, and its architecture boxes can open the files and lines behind them.

scenes.text: Pick a box and trace everything upstream or downstream. Pick a start and an end, and it traces the route between them.
And it's not just for code. It knows ten diagram types, and it'll even map out a job search.
The trick? Claude never draws the picture. It writes a list of boxes and arrows, and Archify's checker bounces anything broken back to Claude. You get one HTML file to share.
scenes.say: The trick? Claude never draws the picture. It writes a list of boxes and arrows, and Arkify's checker bounces anything broken back to Claude. You get one HTML file to share.

scenes.text: The catch: it maps what you ask about, not your whole codebase. And it checks for updates about once a day, unless you turn that off.
Install it with one command, link in the description.
If you like this kind of content, like, share and follow Curiously.
